correctness.rationale: The stationary half-state law pi=(1-p,p) is invariant under an explicitly listed full-branch affine partition. Conditional densities remain uniform on each sign half after every branch history; direct branch accounting gives M_p(z) exactly, so pi M_p(z)^N 1 counts all N-step digit-zero events. The eigenvalue computation and rank-one stochastic decomposition yield the exact geometric covariances, N-variance and sharp h=p(1-p) extremizers. Positive finite-state Perron theory proves the all-real SCGF, Gaussian limit and LDP. The independent standard-library verifier directly pushes actual affine intervals and passed 434 exact tests over rational p and finite N/lag. Tests are corroboration, not proof of infinite results.

value.rationale: Zero-digit frequency was introduced to quantify Hamming weight/cost of signed binary computation; exact finite-count variability and rare frequencies are direct, motivated next-order quantities. The theorem classifies the entire switching-bias interval p in (0,1) at the naturally solvable endpoint alpha=1; the independent-digit exception p=1/2, strictly positive geometric memory at all other biases, and the two sharp variance maxima at p=(1±sqrt(3/5))/2 are structural features not implied by the known marginal. The SCGF and rate endpoints quantify large fluctuations in a mathematical model, without claiming unrelated applications or general alpha.
